entry.label: Transduction in Simondon
entry.description: Simondon's account of individuation through progressive structuring: each formed region helps constitute the next. It differs from converting signals across an organisational boundary.
entry.canonical_definition: Progressive structuring through which an individual takes form; constituted structure enables further structuring.

profile.title: Transduction in Simondon
profile.summary: Crystallisation is Simondon's simplest example. His question concerns the coming-into-being of individuals and relations, rather than starting with two already constituted domains.
profile.canonical_definition: Progressive structuring through which an individual takes form; constituted structure enables further structuring.
profile.why_it_matters: Readers can ask whether an intervention changes a connection between established parties or changes what the parties become. This practical question is an editorial comparison.
key_distinctions: A philosophical account versus a demonstrated organisational mechanism
practice_connections: Name which meaning of transduction an argument requires.
common_misreadings: The shared word establishes a shared theory or historical influence.
open_checks: Applications require their own evidence; this route does not establish a Beer–Simondon lineage.
profile.editorial_note: Primary passages checked for this bounded research pass. Exposition and editorial comparisons remain distinct; named editorial acceptance is not implied by publication.
